verdict.label: Self-serve
verdict.summary: GitHub OAuth apps can be registered instantly in developer settings with no verification required for standard usage.

composioFit.summary: Composio provides a managed GitHub app, but you can bring your own custom app for dedicated rate limits or custom branding.
whyOwnApp: Dedicated rate limits rather than sharing quota across Composio users
Custom branding and app name on the consent screen

phases.name: Register OAuth App
steps: Navigate to developer settings in your GitHub account or organization.
Click on OAuth apps and select Register a new application.
Fill in application name, homepage URL, and callback URL from your Composio auth config.
Register the application and retrieve your Client ID and Client Secret.
phases.handoff: Copy your Client ID and Client Secret into the Composio dashboard to complete the custom auth config.

artefacts.title: GitHub OAuth App Registration Values
artefacts.body:
Application name: [Your App Name]
Homepage URL: https://[yourdomain.com]
Application description: [Brief description of your AI agent integration]
Authorization callback URL: <Composio callback URL from your auth config>

requirements.label: Privacy Policy
requirements.when: Optional for basic custom OAuth apps unless publishing to GitHub Marketplace.

scopes.purpose: Grants full access to public and private repositories including read and write access to code and commit statuses.
Requests an expiring access token and a refresh token.
Grants read/write access to profile info only.

redirectRules.rule: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs in your app settings.

blockers.symptom: Further requests to generate new access tokens will be temporarily blocked, and you may receive error responses.
blockers.cause: Exceeding the limit of 2,000 access token requests per hour.
blockers.fix: Cache tokens and avoid repeatedly signing in users unnecessarily.
blockers.fallback: Use Composio managed app or wait for the hourly rate limit window to reset.

blockers.symptom: Sign in within the same hour requires re-authorization of the application.
blockers.cause: An app signed the user in ten times within one hour, often indicating an infinite loop.
blockers.fix: Debug application authentication flow to stop repeated re-authentications.
blockers.fallback: Re-authorize the application manually when prompted.

checklist.text: Navigate to developer settings in GitHub and start a new OAuth app registration.
Obtain the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard auth config.
Enter the application details and callback URL into GitHub.
Generate and save the Client Secret securely.
Paste Client ID and Client Secret into the Composio dashboard.

uncertainties: Exact approval times for GitHub Marketplace publisher verification if opting to publish publicly rather than use standard custom auth.

claims.text: You can create and register an OAuth app under your personal account or under any organization you have administrative access to.

claims.text: In "Authorization callback URL", type the callback URL of your app.

claims.text: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs. To add additional callback URLs, click Add callback URL .

claims.text: Composio-managed OAuth available? Yes for GITHUB toolkit.
Use your own OAuth app when your product's branding requirements call for it, or when hitting rate limits.
claims.quote: You need your app name on OAuth consent screens. Use your own OAuth app when your product's branding requirements call for it.

claims.text: For OAuth toolkits, register an app in the provider's developer portal and add the redirect URI from the dashboard. Then copy the Client ID and Client Secret back into Composio.
claims.quote: For OAuth toolkits, register an app in the provider's developer portal and add the redirect URI from the dashboard. Then copy the Client ID and Client Secret back into Composio.

claims.text: OAuth apps are subject to a rate limit of 2,000 access token requests per hour.
claims.quote: OAuth apps are subject to a rate limit of 2,000 access token requests per hour .

claims.text: OAuth apps should always cache their tokens, and only rarely need to sign in a user.
claims.quote: OAuth apps should always cache their tokens, and only rarely need to sign in a user.

claims.text: If an app signs the user in ten times within one hour, the next sign in within the same hour will require re-authorization of the application.

claims.text: repo scope grants full access to public and private repositories including read and write access to code.
claims.quote: repo Grants full access to public and private repositories including read and write access to code, commit statuses, repository invitations, collaborators, deployment statuses, and repository webhooks

claims.text: offline_access scope requests an expiring access token and a refresh token.
claims.quote: offline_access Requests an expiring access token and a refresh token, even if your OAuth app is not configured to use expiring tokens.

claims.text: user scope grants read/write access to profile info only.
claims.quote: user Grants read/write access to profile info only. Note that this scope includes user:email and user:follow .
